biteOfDay: ing Trout fishing on Taneycomo has been solid as fall settles in. Rainbows are active throughout the upper stretches and browns are showing strongly in their seasonal push, especially in the first mile below the dam. Anglers are connecting with marabou jigs, scuds, midges, and small streamers. Night fishing with medium streamers or small jerkbaits continues to produce. On Table Rock, bass are hold

tableRock.clarity: Gin-clear near dam; verify arms locally

taneycomo.temp: Tailwater cold (typically ~50–54°F). Verify at the bank.
taneycomo.generation: ~8,552,822 cfs at 12:00 CT (USACE live). Overnight ~20; afternoon peak ~8,552,822. Call SWPA 866-494-1993 before you wad.

species.name: Bass
species.technique: Topwater at dawn; deep spoon, shakey head, deep crank mid-day

species.name: Walleye
species.technique: Crankbaits, live bait (carried mid-summer pattern — not freshly guide-verified 07-21)

species.name: Crappie
species.depth: Deep timber & brush piles (James River/Long Creek arms)
species.technique: Small white or yellow jigs under deep-water docks

species.name: Trout
species.technique: Low-flow morning window; pink worms/jigs/midges; drift when generation heavy (Trophy Area nightcrawlers)

species.name: Bluegill
species.technique: Worms, small poppers — great for kids (mid-summer pattern carry)

species.name: Catfish
species.depth: Indian Point & near dam, shallows after dark
species.technique: Stink bait, hot dogs, cut/frozen bait — evening/night

tip: Insider tip: Use the minimal early-morning flows on Taneycomo. Wade or drift seams and current breaks with a 1/16- to 1/8-oz marabou micro jig in black, sculpin, olive or with an orange head, a zebra midge (#16–20 in red or black), or a scud. When generation increases later, switch to weighted rigs
